title: Sewn cast-off
subtitle: A darning-needle cast-off that mimics the look of the Kitchener graft.
excerpt: The sewn cast-off works with a darning needle to create a cast-off chain that closely resembles knit stitches. The most elastic standard finishing edge for ribbing and cuffs.
sourceNotes: Technique documented as 'sewn bind-off' in twentieth-century knitting literature. Related to the grafting or Kitchener method described in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938).

glossaryTerms.definition: A cast-off method using a darning needle to draw the yarn through stitches in two passes, creating a chain that looks like knit stitches and stretches as generously as the ribbing beneath.

content.text: uses a darning needle to close the last row. Threading the yarn through stitches in two passes creates a chain that stretches freely and looks like a knit stitch from the right side. Elizabeth Zimmermann published the method widely, though the two-pass sewing approach appears in earlier British needlework literature. Difficulty: intermediate.
Your finished piece with live stitches on the needle
A cut tail about three times the width of the cast-off edge
Cut the yarn, leaving a tail three times the width of the piece. Thread it onto the darning needle.
With the knitting needle in the left hand, insert the darning needle through the first two stitches from right to left (purlwise through both). Do not remove them from the knitting needle.
Now insert the darning needle through the first stitch only, from left to right (knitwise). Slip this stitch off the knitting needle.
Repeat steps 2 and 3 to the end of the row. Fasten off the last stitch with a small sewn anchor.

The sewn cast-off suits any edge that needs to stretch with the body: sock cuffs in 1x1 or 2x2 ribbing, glove tops, and necklines. Where the standard cast-off grips, this one stretches, making it the right choice when a hat brim or sock cuff must pull over a wider part.

items.symptom: Cast-off chain looks loose and loopy
items.fix: Snug each stitch gently as you slip it off the knitting needle. The two-pass tension determines the finished look.

items.cause: Working the purlwise pass too tightly in step 2
items.fix: Let the darning needle travel through both stitches loosely. The tension comes from step 3, not step 2.

items.symptom: Tail too short to complete the cast-off
items.fix: Measure three times the width of the cast-off edge. For a hat brim of 60 cm circumference, that is 180 cm of tail. Add 20 cm for threading and the end.
